sections.text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: It is hard to see this vision of Me that thou hast seen. Even the most powerful have longed for it in vain.
नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया।
Not by study of the scriptures, or by austerities, not by gifts or sacrifices, is it possible to see Me as thou hast done.
Only by tireless devotion can I be seen and known; only thus can a man become one with Me, O Arjuna!

We have been discussing chapter 11, Viswarupadarsana yoga -- the Yoga of Revelation of the Cosmic Form. We have seen in this chapter that Bhagavan showed his cosmic form. So what does that mean? The cosmic form is that form which includes all the forms in this cosmos, in this world, in this Jagat. All the forms at one place, from past, present, and future.
So that negates time. If there is no past, present and future, there is no time. If there is only one entity, one supreme being, then there is no time. I dont require any time to meet myself. I am always there, so there is no time required. It is when I have to meet somebody else, then I have to have time.
The two, it requires time and we can say well meet at 10 o clock every Sunday morning. So as long as there are more than one, there will be time. If theres only one, there is no time. So in this cosmic form, everything is crunched into one. Past, present, future. There is no time also.
If there is one, there is no space. If there is one dot, the dot doesnt require any space. Instead of two dots, there is a distance between the two and theres space between the two. The space is created only when there are two. So in this, all forms are in one. Therefore there is no space also.
Because all forms are within that one form, that one form now becomes the form, the cosmic form. And therefore there is no space. So the space and time are both negated. In cosmic form, to have any form, what you require is space and time. Without space and time, there is no form. So the actual vision that Arjuna had was that of a formless space, supreme being.
But then he describes all these beings in it: I see Brahma, I see Vishnu, I see all the Siddhas, I see all Rakshasas, I see Dhritarashtras sons. So in the supreme, all the probabilities -- infinite probabilities, the infinite amount of forms you can imagine -- you can create in that infinite.
It is something like if one of my clients comes to me and says, Rajan, here is a piece of land. Design a building. I say, But what kind of a building? What do you want to use it for? If you leave everything up to me, I have infinite possibilities -- what I can design, what type of building I can design.
There I can say, it can be a hospital, it can be a jail. It can be an office building, a multi-storied office building. Maybe its a single-story office building. No, no, it can be residential. Well, maybe multi-story. infinite possibilities.
To really design a building, I have to eliminate all other possibilities and narrow it down to one. It cant be a hospital because its not possible here, not needed here. It cannot be a jail because we have no authority to imprison anybody. I have to come down to negate everything until only one choice remains, and that becomes my choice. So for any form, its necessary that you negate all other forms.
So when I say, lets say Prakashji comes to the room and I see Prakashji -- what I have to do is negate all 7 billion people on this planet. All remaining 7 billion people are not that; thats Prakashji. So to create a form from a probability of infinite probabilities in the supreme, I have to negate all other probabilities. Here, Arjuna can see whatever he wants to see. So is the case with us, because we see from a narrow perspective, we negate things, and it comes down to a particular form. So here Bhagavan showed Arjuna the supreme form which is formless but has infinite probabilities and possibilities of forms.
So that was the reason. And therefore Arjuna could see things which are delightful and those which are frightful. When it comes to the delightful, when we think about God as divine, it is very pleasant. But when we think about God who is also responsible for -- or also enabling -- the evil in this world, that is very frightful. Therefore we say, Bhagavan, I dont want to see that part of yours. Show me something which I can live with.
So thats what we have seen so far. Arjuna requested, put me back where I was before. So Bhagavan showed him the same Swarupa as Vasudeva, as Vasudevas son which he was before as his charioteer. And then Bhagavan told him, look, this form of mine which you have seen -- which has all the forms included from past, present, and future -- is very difficult to see. It is auspicious but very difficult to see. And therefore nobody has seen it before.
You have seen it simply because of my grace -- Atma Yogat. By my yoga I could make you see this. But it is not possible to see through all the other preparations. Learning Veda, Dhyana, Yajna -- these are means but not the goal. You cannot achieve the goal by just preparing for it. Na aham vedena tapasa na danena ijyaya shakya evam vidho drastum -- as you have seen me, it is not possible through study of Vedas or austerities or charities or even sacrifices.
It almost looks like Bhagavan is discouraging us -- none of this is going to be helpful. But Bhagavan is actually making a statement of fact. We can learn from this verse the secret of success in anything. Can I become a successful architect just by going to architecture school? Many of my classmates are in the United States.
They all went to the same school. We all got the architecture degree. None of them are practicing architecture. Theyre successful in what they are doing. They own motels, they own gas stations and big houses and many cars. But theyre not practicing architecture.
So just by going to architecture school, I cannot become a successful architect. So is the case with doctors, engineers. What makes a person a successful professional? The first thing is his devotion to the profession. He has to be devoted to his profession. When I came to this country -- big recession time, 1982, huge recession -- I was in Houston.
Pipe drafting was a big thing there because of all the oil companies. And people said, forget about architecture, do pipe drafting, you will make a lot of money. And I said, theres one thing I will not do, and that is leave architecture. Ill find jobs somewhere. Even drafting in architecture is acceptable, but not pipe drafting. So unless you are devoted to a profession -- thats the first requirement -- but even that doesnt make me successful as a designer of buildings, because I need the grace of my clients.
I may be the best architect on this planet, but if there is no client that I can convince to let me design his or her building, then I wont be able to design. So to become a successful architect who can design a building and construct it, I need the grace of my clients. The ultimate thing I need is grace from the one from whom I am seeking that work, that achievement. But to get there, I have to do a lot more. I cant really just come out and say, Im devoted to architecture, give me work.
Thats also not possible. You have to train yourself continuously. So that you become proficient and efficient. Then somebody will see that you are capable of doing so. So Bhagavan said, two things I require. One is your devotion to your goal.
And then grace from whoever is the fruit giver. Whoever is responsible to give you that work or that achievement. So Bhagavan says, Na aham vedair tapasa na danena ijyaya shakya evam vidho drastum drishtavanasi mam yatha -- you have seen me, but I am not possible to be seen through all these things alone. We think that preparing ourselves is good enough. But when it is not good enough, what you require is: Bhaktya tu ananyaya shakya aham evam vidho Arjuna jnatum drastum cha tattvena praveshtum cha parantapa.
It is not possible by just preparation. If you are devoted to me -- Bhaktya tu Ananyaya -- by single-minded devotion, it is possible. Bhagavan has given you the secret. What you really require is single-pointed devotion. And devotion, as we have discussed many times, is nothing but love for the divine. And love is nothing but identification.
I love someone because I identify with that person. Because I identify with this class. I like to discuss Bhagavad Gita. You like to discuss Bhagavad Gita. I love people who come to this class. So this identification is love.
I dont love my neighbours child. As much as I love my own child. I identify with my child, my son. So love is nothing but pure identification. Without identification you cannot love anything or any being. So love for the divine is devotion.
But I cannot love the divine without knowing the divine. And therefore Bhagavan spent the last five chapters defining what the divine is, culminating in this Vishwaroop Pradarshan. So Bhagavan says it is possible. And then Bhagavan gives the steps of that vision: Jnatum drastum cha tattvena praveshtum cha parantapa.
First you have to know. For identifying with anyone. I need to know that person. I have to know that person. I cant fall in love with a girl who I never met. I have to know her first.
So jnatum -- knowing first. In our studies we say the first is Shravanam -- listen to the scriptures, listen to the nature of the Lord. This is what we are doing. We are listening from Bhagavan. Then you will see me.
Then you will know me. You will see me in my essence. Wherever I look, I see you. So thats the vision -- Drastum. In our path, through Mananam (reflection), I create a perception of what I have learned. Bhagavans form is like that.
And then I reflect on it. Have you seen calendar pictures of Vishwarup Darshan? The painters created those iconic images weve all seen -- Bhagavan with many heads and many arms and fire coming out of his mouth. Of course, painters have their limitations. But if you have listened to the five chapters carefully and then you reflect on it, then Bhagavan says, you will see me in my essence.
The last stage is Praveshtum -- then you will identify with me. Pravesham is to become one, to enter into that self. Right now, I am in my limited being. Im completely identified with this body, this mind, this intellect.
My identification is so complete that there is no real rivalry between my right hand and left hand, my right leg and left leg. That is complete identification with this limited self -- i.e., praveshtum, entered into that me. Bhagavan says, if you reflect on that Vishwaroop, then you will also enter into that. You will identify with that supreme as you identify with your limited self right now. Here the operative word is Ananya Bhakti.
With single minded devotion, you shall be able to know me. You shall be able to see me. You shall be able to enter into me. The last word he gives us how to do that. So first he says, this vision is not possible without my grace. But it is possible if you are single mindedly devoted to me.
But how can I develop that single-minded devotion? Bhagavan answers in the last verse of this chapter. Mat Karma Krit -- the very first thing he says is, do everything for me. Continue doing everything youre doing right now. You think youre doing it for you, youre doing it for your family, youre doing it for your country. He says, just think -- its all me.

Krishna now reveals the secret: Only by tireless devotion can I be seen and known; only thus can a man become one with Me. The word used is ananya bhakti - single-pointed, exclusive devotion. This is followed by a progression: know Me (jnatum), see Me (drastum), and enter into Me (praveshtum). These correspond to the traditional steps of shravana (hearing), manana (reflection), and nididhyasana (meditation/absorption). Knowledge comes first, then vision, then complete identification.
The key insight is that devotion (bhakti) is not mere emotion but deep identification. We love what we identify with - our children, our work, our country. Love and identification go together. To develop devotion to the divine requires knowing the divine (hence chapters 7-10 describing Krishnas nature), then seeing the divine in the world (the vision of chapter 11), and finally entering into complete identification where the sense of separation dissolves entirely.
For todays practice, work with the concept of ananya - single-pointed, without another. Examine where your devotion currently goes. Most of us are devoted to many things: comfort, success, approval, security, pleasure. These divided devotions scatter our energy. What would it mean to have all these secondary devotions organized under one primary devotion - to truth, to the divine, to consciousness itself? Begin by noticing when you serve lesser gods throughout the day. Each choice for immediate gratification over deeper truth is a moment of divided devotion.
